name: Bayesian Analysis of Retinotopic Maps
summary: Refines measured pRF maps with an anatomical retinotopy prior (Benson & Winawer 2018) using neuropythy, producing smoothed polar angle, eccentricity and size maps and visual-area labels.
description: Projects measured pRF surface maps onto the FreeSurfer surfaces and runs neuropythy register_retinotopy to fit a Bayesian retinotopic model that combines the measurements with an anatomical prior. Use it after a pRF mapping App to reduce noise and label visual areas V1-V3 and beyond. Needs the FreeSurfer subject and pRF output with surface maps.

inputs.description: FreeSurfer subject directory of the same subject.
Measured pRF maps (r2, polar angle, eccentricity, rfWidth) including surface maps.

outputs.description: Inferred pRF maps (polar angle, eccentricity, rfWidth, visual area) in volume and on the surface (curv and GIFTI).
Volumetric parcellation into visual areas (key in key.txt).

citations.text: Benson NC, Winawer J. Bayesian analysis of retinotopic maps. eLife 7:e40224 (2018).
Benson NC, et al. The retinotopic organization of striate cortex is well predicted by surface topology. Curr Biol 22(21):2081-2085 (2012).

Benson NC, et al. Correction of distortion in flattened representations of the cortical surface allows prediction of V1-V3 functional organization from anatomy. PLoS Comput Biol 10(3):e1003538 (2014).

failure_modes.fix: Check that the pRF input has surface maps for the same FreeSurfer subject.
